label: Ryanmen Protorun
description: Block theory: choose the discard that keeps the ryanmen wait.

label: Bulging Float
description: Block theory: the bulging float is a real decision — keep it for two runs, or break it for a better block or wait.

label: Protorun Priority
description: Block theory: break the closed wait and keep both side waits.

label: Ryankan Break
description: Block theory: keep the new side wait and break the double closed shape.

label: Protorun Plus One
description: Block theory: keep the cover on the weaker protorun and break the strong side wait's cover instead.

label: Nobetan: Keep 3456
description: Block theory: keep the stretched single even though breaking it accepts more tiles, because the kept shape leaves far more side-wait completions.

label: Pair Count
description: Block theory: a third pair is weaker than the side wait it was drawn from.

label: Skipping Shape
description: Block theory: a float two ranks from a run is worth more than an isolated float of the same rank, so keep the skipping tile.

label: Pair Count: Pon Planned
description: Block theory: with a dragon pair to Pon, keep three pairs and break the closed wait.

label: Perfect 1-Away
description: Block theory: keep the perfect 1-away (two side waits, two pairs) instead of the draw that accepts slightly more tiles.

label: Chiitoitsu vs Toitoi
description: Yaku pursuit: a pair just became a set. Stay with chiitoitsu when a pair is futile; otherwise keep the set and build toitoi.

book.label: ch5.5 · How to get toitoi / chiitoitsu

label: Sanshoku Pursuit
description: Ch. 5.1 floating method: keep the floating tile for sanshoku only when the hand has no other yaku or dora; otherwise take the side-wait pinfu.

label: Chiitoitsu Riichi vs Dama
description: Seven pairs: decide whether to declare Riichi or stay dama.

label: Riichi Judgement
description: The ch. 7 rule: Riichi if you have a han, a good wait, or the deal.

book.section_title: To riichi or not to riichi?
book.label: ch7.1 · To riichi or not to riichi?

label: Dama: Bad Wait
description: Ch. 7 bad wait: Riichi with three or more live winning tiles, dama with one or two simple ones, but Riichi on an honor or terminal.

label: Dama: Genbutsu Wait
description: Ch. 7 genbutsu wait: a riichi threat has already discarded one of your winning tiles, so the players folding to them throw it.

label: Dama: Expensive Hand
description: Ch. 7 high scoring hand: the worst winning tile already scores 7700, so dama is fine and haneman+ means no riichi.

label: Dama: Improving Hand
description: Ch. 7 improving hand: an early ready hand with many improving draws stays dama instead of declaring Riichi.

label: Riichi: Immediate Suji Trap
description: Ch. 8 suji trap: two discards leave the same wait, but only one makes the winning tile a suji of the declaration tile.

label: Added Kan Decision
description: Open Pon, fourth tile drawn: decide whether to upgrade to an Added Kan or discard.

label: Concealed Quad Decision
description: Four concealed copies: declare the concealed quad only when the hand is close to ready, never when the fourth copy is a good floating tile.

label: Wind Discard Order
description: First turn with two or three valueless winds: throw the right player's wind first.

label: Meld or Not
description: A Pon is offered on a cheap and slow hand: pass, unless the book's exceptions apply.

book.section_title: To meld or not to meld?
book.label: ch9.1 · To meld or not to meld?

label: Open Quad Decision
description: An opponent discards the fourth copy of your dragon triplet: call the open quad only when the hand's value, the placement, or the score line asks for it.

label: AI Hotseat
description: Mortal plays all four seats of a round; you take over one seat at a random decision that actually occurred, and are graded by Mortal's own choice there.

label: Defense: Fold to Riichi
description: An opponent has declared Riichi against a junk hand: discard the one tile the book calls 100% safe.

label: Push or Fold
description: Ch. 8.1 push/fold: a 1-away hand may push only with both a high score and a good wait; otherwise fold to the safest tile.

book.label: ch8.1 · To push or to fold?

label: Defense: Safest Discard
description: An opponent has declared Riichi: discard the tile the book's safety chart ranks safest.

label: Defense: Suji / No-Chance Ranking
description: The safest tile is a suji or no-chance tile: rank the hand on the book's table, where the runner-up is exactly one row worse.

label: Defense: No-Chance Tile
description: A complete blockade hides the only safe tile: every side wait needs one of the four visible copies, so the neighbour is no chance.

label: Defense: One-Chance Tile
description: An incomplete blockade leaves one last copy: in the early turns the chart ranks the neighbour above every non-suji tile.

label: Defense: Double One-Chance Tile
description: Two incomplete blockades on the same wait: the opponent needs the last copy of both protorun tiles, which is safer than a single one chance.

label: Defense: Blockade + Suji
description: Neither theory is enough alone: a complete blockade denies one side wait and a genbutsu denies the other, so the middle tile is safe.

label: Defense: Nothing Is Safe
description: No tile is identified as safe: apply the book's fallback and break up the pair.

label: Defense: Two or More Threats
description: Several opponents are live at once — two Riichi declarations, a Riichi plus a three-meld open hand, or all three: discard the one tile the book calls safe against everyone, not the one that is merely safe against one.

label: Open Hand: Post-Chi Discard
description: An opponent with three open melds chi'd, then discarded: read whether the neighbourhood of that discard is safe or dangerous.

label: Pinfu: Build the Head
description: The head is still open: keep the terminals and valueless winds, because the value honor can never be the pinfu head.

label: Honitsu: Commit or Efficiency
description: Ch. 5.4: five blocks in one suit plus honors is not enough on its own — commit to honitsu only when the plan is worth more than the hand played straight.
